correctness.rationale: A direct coalition bound gives the incoming-weight core; the complement-coalition identity forces uniqueness. A random arrival ordering for one recipient determines the Shapley share for the recipient and for each incoming neighbor. Summation gives a precise Shapley/core difference as a column-stochastic graph operator applied to the positive recipient-weight vector; the irreducible operator has exactly one positive projective fixed ray. All three indegree cases follow, including zero-coordinate impossibility. Undirected reciprocal specialization is a graph Laplacian, with strictly negative Dirichlet energy unless each component is regular. The standard-library independent definition-based checker passed exact calculations on 771 labeled connected undirected graphs and exact directed examples. No numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The trust-game literature identifies potential conflict between a fair Shapley allocation and the unique stable core. For recipient-dependent but homogeneous incoming assessments, a mathematically natural network-design restriction, the theorem fully resolves existence of stable/fair trust scores, forbids positive calibration on mixed indegree-one topologies, and uniquely prescribes the balancing weights via a reverse-walk stationary law on all-positive indegree-at-least-two topologies. The reciprocal result classifies every uniform-weight graph and supplies a concrete blocking coalition/energy certificate. It is a natural structural compatibility and design result, not a textbook substitution or arbitrary parameter table.
